thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — noticed a regression in paged-KV runs with FlashA variants on 8k seqs. p95 jumped ~2.5x after the allocator change.
kevin: ugh. which allocator change? the slab->segmented-slab one? :thinking:
maria: yeah, landed yesterday. The block table growth pattern changed; we see many tiny allocations and fragmentation. profiler logs attached below.
ashok: can you paste the perf numbers? quick compare to before.
maria: Sure — short snippet from perf run (same rig, A100s):
```
p50: 11.8ms
p95: 118.2ms  <-- old was 48ms
p99: 447.3ms
tokens/sec: 1.18k
kv_page_faults: 392/s
block_table_entries: 1.4M
frag_ratio: 0.27
```
sasha: kv_page_faults that high explains it. Are pages larger now? page_size change?
maria: page_size unchanged (64KB). The allocator now returns many small block-table slabs (4KB pages) which increases TLB churn when scanning for eviction.
kevin: hmm TLB + memcpy loops can kill FlashAttention variants that expect contiguous KV chunks. Did kernel selection fallback to fused version or still FlashA?
maria: still FlashA-v2 by default. When we force fallback to fused matmul-attn, latency goes down for long sequences but CPU overhead up for short ones.
lisa: can we add a quick heuristic: if block_table_frag > 0.2 or kv_page_faults > 200/s then prefer fused-attn or precompact table?
ashok: I sketched a heuristic yesterday. Pseudocode:
```
if seq_len > 2048 and kv_pf_rate > 150:
  select_kernel = fused_attn
elif batch_size >= 16 and avg_token_len < 256:
  select_kernel = flash_fastpath
else:
  select_kernel = flash_fallback
```
kevin: also consider a prefetch window: when evicting, prefetch next N pages into a contiguous staging buffer if seq_len spikes. That reduces random memcpy.
maria: ran microbench with prefetch=4 and contiguous staging: p95 dropped from 118ms -> 62ms, p99 -> 230ms. Still above old, but much better.
perf-bot: ALERT: regression_detected: paged-kv/flashA-regression -- delta_p95=+146% -- ticket created (#INFR-3121)
sasha: thanks perf-bot. Let's avoid rolling back allocator; try patch: (1) compact block table allocator for hot shards, (2) kernel-selection heuristic, (3) staged prefetch for page faults.
maria: implemented prototype for compact-on-hot-shard. Quick config snippet:
```
kv_pager:
  page_size: 64kb
  slab_compact_threshold: 0.2
  hot_shard_compact: true
  prefetch_pages: 4
  kernel_policy:
    pf_rate_threshold: 150
    seq_len_threshold: 2048
```
kevin: can you run the regression harness with that config and the cross-model matrix? include LLama-variants & GPT-style.
maria: running now. baseline->patch comparison looks promising for gpt-like models. one oddity: smaller models (1B) regress slightly due to extra compaction cost.
lisa: maybe only enable compact-on-hot for models > 6B or when sustained p99>250ms.
ashok: Also we should fix block table allocation strategy: switch to chunked-power-of-two slabs for block metadata to reduce fragmentation. That avoids expensive compaction in many cases.
kevin: agreed. chunked-power-of-two gives O(1) free list per size class. Less metadata overhead. Are there concurrency issues with compaction and eviction?
maria: compaction runs under eviction lock per shard; cheap if we limit frequency. compaction cost measured ~8-12ms per run on hot shard.
sasha: timeline? if we land heuristic + prefetch + chunk allocator, can we ship a canary tomorrow to dedicated clusters?
maria: yes. PRs: allocator chunking (WIP), prefetch + kernel policy (ready), compaction guard (WIP). I'll coordinate with deploy.
deploy-bot: canary window scheduled: eng-runtime-canary 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC -> 2h
maria: thanks. I'll attach the full profiler trace to the ticket. TL;DR: regression introduced by allocator change, mitigated by combining compacting heuristics, prefetching, and kernel selection policy. Need to tune thresholds per model family.
kevin: sounds good. if the canary looks green we'll backport to dedicated. Also add a regression test in perf-harness that flips allocator modes.
sasha: agreed. I'll own rolling change to policy config after canary. :+1:
maria: ping me for any follow-ups, I'll keep logs in the ticket.
